cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes '=ERFC.PRECISE(1)' with the result 0.15729921. Re-derived independently with mpmath at 50 decimal digits: erfc(1) = 0.15729920705028513066, which rounds to the published 0.15729921 at 8 dp. It is also exactly 1 - erf(1) = 1 - 0.84270079294971486934, the identity the two pages' own examples encode.

The ERFC and ERFC.PRECISE pages carry identical descriptions ("Returns the complementary ERF function integrated between x and infinity"), identical single-argument syntax and the identical published example result 0.15729921, so their difference is exactly zero.

cases.description: The complementary error function at zero
cases.expected_note: Derived from the documented definition: integrated from 0 to infinity, the complementary error function is exactly 1.
Excel documents: "If x is nonnumeric, ERFC.PRECISE returns the #VALUE! error value."
